derivation: from G4206 (πόῤῥω) with adverbial enclitic of source;
def: from far, or (by implication) at a distance, i.e. distantly

occurrences.text: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
